title: Energy and Speed
seo_title: Grade 4 Energy and Speed Worksheets: Energy of Motion and Ramp Investigations
standard_text: Use evidence to construct an explanation relating the speed of an object to the energy of that object.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on energy and speed (NGSS 4-PS3-1): energy of motion, faster objects have more energy, and ramp investigations with data tables. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: The faster an object moves, the more energy it has.
key_sub: A moving object has energy of motion. A faster ball can push a cup farther than the same ball moving slowly.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy is the ability to make things move or change. A moving object has energy of motion.

The faster an object moves, the more energy it has. A fast ball can push a cup farther, ring a bell louder or sting your hand more than the same ball moving slowly.

Example

The same ball starts at 10 cm and at 30 cm on a ramp. Which start pushes the cup farther?

Higher start = faster ball.

Faster ball = more energy.

Answer: the 30 cm start

Example

A bike slows from fast to slow. What happens to its energy of motion?

Slower means less energy of motion.

Answer: It decreases.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a bigger object always has more energy. Compare the same object at different speeds.
  • Thinking speed and energy are not connected. Faster means more energy.
  • Changing more than one thing in a ramp test.

faq.q: How is speed related to energy?
faq.a: The faster an object moves, the more energy of motion it has. The same ball rolling fast has more energy than when it rolls slowly.

faq.q: Does an object that is not moving have energy of motion?
faq.a: No. Energy of motion depends on motion. A ball sitting still has no energy of motion.

faq.q: How can you show that faster objects have more energy?
faq.a: Roll the same ball down a ramp from different heights. The higher start makes the ball faster, and it pushes a cup farther.

items.e: Faster motion means more energy of motion.

items.q: Leo says a big slow truck must always have more energy of motion than a small fast truck. Why is his claim not supported by speed alone?
c: Speed also matters, so you must compare the same object at different speeds.
items.e: In grade 4 we compare the same object at different speeds to see that speed changes energy.
